draft.title: Why wellbeing differs between places
card: Wellbeing is how well people's lives are going, including health, income, education and safety. It differs from place to place because people do not all have the same access to the things that support it.
Access
Jobs give income. Services such as health care and schools support health and learning. Clean water protects people from disease. Education leads to more skills and more choices.
Causes behind access

History, such as colonisation or past trade, can shape who holds wealth and services. Environment, such as drought, floods or distance, can make it harder to grow food or build roads. Conflict can destroy homes, schools and hospitals.
Government

Government choices decide where money is spent, such as on schools, clinics, water supply and roads. Two places with similar environments can have different wellbeing if their governments make different choices.
draft.remember: Wellbeing differs where access to jobs, services, water and education differs, and history, environment, conflict and government choices all help to explain why.

a.q: Which of these best explains why wellbeing is often lower in a region with no clean water supply?
opts: People are more exposed to disease, which harms health
People earn lower incomes because they work fewer hours
People choose to spend less time in school
People live too far from the sea to travel
a.why: Clean water protects people from disease, so a place without it tends to have poorer health. The income option is tempting, but the card does not link water to hours worked, and a lack of access is not a personal choice.
a.clue: Think about what clean water protects people from.

b.q: Two nearby districts have similar rainfall and soils. District A has many clinics and schools. District B has few, because its government spent less there. Which statement best explains why wellbeing is likely to differ?
opts: Government choices led to different access to services
Environment is the only cause of the difference
Conflict between the districts has caused the gap
History is the only cause of wellbeing differences
b.why: The environments are similar, so the difference comes from government choices that gave District A better access to clinics and schools. Environment is the tempting answer, but the case rules it out. Nothing in the case mentions conflict, and history is not the cause the case describes.
b.clue: The districts share an environment, so look at who decides where services go.

a.best: People are more exposed to disease, which harms health

b.best: Government choices led to different access to services

problems.detail: The stem already gives the answer: it says District B has few clinics and schools 'because its government spent less there', so students can pick the government option without understanding the idea. The clue ('look at who decides where services go') points to it again.

Two distractors use 'only' ('History is the only cause...', 'Environment is the only cause...'), while the card says these factors 'can' shape wellbeing. The absolute wording makes them easy to rule out on form alone.
